comment: The ubiquitous language. One concept, one name. Edit here; docs/ubiquitous-language.md is generated from this file and tools/check_language.py enforces it.

orthography.comment: The same concept is spelled for its layer: British in prose and UI copy, the technical spelling in identifiers. Neither layer may mix the two.

prose.why: Prose and UI copy are British English; a cost centre and a budget centre are spelled with -re.

code.why: Identifiers, JSON and SQL use the same -re spelling as the prose, so a search for the concept finds one word in every layer.

terms.definition: One business date's cash book, opened and closed as a unit.
One income or expense movement in a cash book day.
An instruction to pay one recipient one amount, approved before it is paid.
A batch of approved payment orders exported as one SEPA credit-transfer file.
A batch of receivables collected under mandates as one SEPA direct-debit file.
A debtor's authorisation to collect, with its sequence type and reference.
An amount owed by a debtor, collected by a collection run or settled another way.
A CAMT or MT940 file imported against a cash account.
A collection or transfer the bank sent back, releasing the receivable it settled.
One reminder issued to a debtor at a dunning level.
A step in the dunning chain, priced by amount bands.
A foundation whose funds are administered in its own books.
One year's book of a foundation, carried over into the next year.
Posting a foundation book's net as the next year's opening movement.
A budget line identified by year, chapter and title, carrying its allocation.
Where a position's money comes from: a chapter and title, a funder or a foundation.
Who administers a position's money.
An amount reserved on a budget position before it is spent.
An order to a supplier, approved before goods are received.
The recorded delivery of ordered goods, with the quantity received.
A party the product orders goods or services from.
A supplier's invoice received and matched to an order.
A structured invoice in UBL, CII or ebInterface form.
An organisational unit that carries costs.
What a cost is: the nature of the expense.
The product, service or project a cost is carried to.
Distributing a cost centre's costs onto receivers by a key.
The internal price per unit at which a cost centre bills its service.
One KLR movement booked on a cost centre.
A definition plus its rows, rendered as a file or a screen.
A stored file produced by a report, export or document render.
A value in a namespace the product reads but does not own.
A permission set a principal holds.
The authenticated identity a request carries.
